newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Gulf Investment Corp says '96 net up 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Investment Corp says '96 net up 6.0 pct.

text.p: Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corp (GIC), equally owned by six Gulf Arab states, on Monday reported a 6.0 percent rise in calendar 1996 net profit to $122.9 million.
GIC's "combined net profit for 1996 amounted to $122.9 million," said a statement issued after a general assembly meeting held in Bahrian on Sunday.
The profit makes a 16.4 percent return on the paid-up capital of GIC, it said.
Total assets rose to $10.5 billion in 1996 from 10.2 billion in 1995, it said.

Thirteen-year-old GIC was set by the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- a political and economic alliance that groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar -- to fund projects in member states to help deversify their economy from oil.
Its activities also include commercial banking and investment management.
